cells: Syiem of Hima Nongkhlaw; led the Anglo-Khasi War (1829-33); died in British captivity, 17 July 1835 — commemorated as U Tirot Sing Day (Chapter 3)
First Chief Minister of Meghalaya (from 1972); also led the 1970-72 autonomous-state administration (Chapter 4)

Prominent Meghalaya political leader; former Speaker of the Lok Sabha; founder of the Nationalist Congress Party (with others) and later the National People's Party; father of current CM Conrad Sangma
Current (2026) Chief Minister of Meghalaya (NPP), continuously in office since 6 March 2018; son of P.A. Sangma (Chapter 5)

blocks.content: ★ EXAM POINT: Conrad Sangma is the son of P.A. Sangma, a former Lok Sabha Speaker and founder of the National People's Party (NPP) — a useful family-political-legacy fact linking two generations of Meghalaya's most prominent political family.

items: Meghalaya: approx 22,429 sq km; borders Assam and Bangladesh; capital: Shillong; means 'Abode of Clouds'.
Three hill divisions: Garo (west), Khasi (centre), Jaintia (east); highest point: Shillong Peak (~1,965 m).
Mawsynram = highest average annual rainfall on Earth; Cherrapunji (Sohra) = highest rainfall in a single month/year (1861).
Living root bridges (Nongriat's Double-Decker bridge); Krem Liat Prah = India's longest cave system.
Khasi Hills: decentralised 'Hima' chiefdoms (e.g. Khyrim, Mylliem), each led by a Syiem; Jaintia Hills: centralised Jaintia kingdom; Garo Hills: clan-based, Nokma-led, no centralised kingdom.
Anglo-Khasi War (1829-33): U Tirot Sing's resistance; captured 1833, died in captivity 17 July 1835 (U Tirot Sing Day).
Autonomous state within Assam from 2 April 1970; full statehood 21 January 1972 (with Manipur and Tripura).
Sixth Schedule ADCs: KHADC (Shillong), JHADC (Jowai), GHADC (Tura) — operate alongside the state government.
60-seat Assembly: 55 ST-reserved seats. Current CM: Conrad Sangma (NPP, since 6 March 2018); Governor: C.H. Vijayashankar (since 30 July 2024).
Coal ('rat-hole mining', banned by NGT 2014) and limestone are key minerals; Khasi Mandarin orange and Lakadong turmeric are GI-tagged products.
Population (2011) approx 29.67 lakh; ST share approx 86%; Christian share approx 75%.
Khasi/Garo = matrilineal (property/lineage via mother; youngest daughter inherits) but NOT matriarchal (political institutions historically male-led).
Khasi/Jaintia languages = Austroasiatic; Garo language = Tibeto-Burman — different families despite shared matriliny.
Wangala (Garo), Shad Suk Mynsiem (Khasi), Behdienkhlam (Jaintia) = flagship community festivals.
Nokrek Biosphere Reserve hosts Citrus indica (wild citrus ancestor) and the red panda; Balpakram National Park is culturally significant to the Garo.
Revise this chapter last — it consolidates every numeric/name/date fact from Chapters 1-10 in one place for rapid recall.
The single most frequently confused fact pair: Mawsynram (highest AVERAGE annual rainfall) vs Cherrapunji (highest rainfall in a single MONTH/YEAR) — never state these as the same record.
Always verify current officeholders (Governor, CM) closer to your exam date.
